question: A shopkeeper took a loan of ₹7500 from a bank on 1 April 2025 with simple interest at 9% per annum. He decided to clear the loan on 1 September 2025. How much amount did he pay back to the bank?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Time duration from 1st April to 1st September = 5 months = 5 ÷ 12 years.

Simple Interest = Principal × Rate × Time

SI = 7500 × 9% × (5 ÷ 12) = ₹281.25

Total Amount = Principal + SI = 7500 + 281.25 = ₹7781.25

**∴ The correct answer is ₹7781.25.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal (P) = ₹7500

Rate of Interest (R) = 9% per annum

Loan start date = 1 April 2025

Loan clear date = 1 September 2025

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

Amount (A) = P + SI

 
• 
 
 
 
 
 1 Apr 2025
 P = ₹7500
 
 1 Sep 2025
 Amount = ?
 
 

 Time = 5 Months (5/12 Year)
 
 Rate = 9% p.a.
 
 SI = ₹281.25 → Amount = ₹7781.25

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total duration from 1 April 2025 to 1 September 2025 is exactly 5 full months.

⇒ Time (T) in years = 5 ÷ 12 years.

⇒ SI = (7500 × 9 × 5) ÷ (100 × 12)

⇒ SI = (75 × 45) ÷ 12

⇒ SI = 3375 ÷ 12

⇒ SI = ₹281.25

⇒ Total Amount = Principal + SI

⇒ Total Amount = 7500 + 281.25

⇒ Total Amount = ₹7781.25

**∴ The correct answer is ₹7781.25.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Conversion of Time

When the time given is in months or days, it must be converted to years for simple interest formulas. Divide months by 12 and days by 365.

Counting Days

When calculating exact days for simple interest, it is standard practice to exclude either the day the money is borrowed or the day it is returned, but not both.

Simple Interest vs Compound Interest

For the first year (or unit time period), Simple Interest and Compound Interest are identical. From the second period onwards, Compound Interest is calculated on the accumulated interest as well as the principal.
